channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Taliban Fighter Confesses to Killing 14 in Panjshir, Accused of War Crimes
item.description: A Taliban fighter confessed to killing 14 people in Panjshir, Afghanistan, to a British tourist. The fighter implied killing non-Muslims was easy. Critics described the confession as evidence of war crimes and crimes against humanity, stating it represents a fraction of the Taliban's alleged atrocities.

item.title: Iran Raises Issue of Closed Shia Institutions with Taliban
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson stated that the country has raised the issue of closed Shia institutions in Afghanistan with the Taliban. Recent closures by the Taliban include religious, educational, and cultural institutions, as well as a clinic supported by Iran in western Kabul. Some officials from these institutions have been detained.

item.title: At Least Six Nations May Join 'Mecca Pact' Following Houthi Attack
item.description: At least six countries may join the 'Mecca Pact', signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. The pact considers an attack on one member an attack on all. An emergency meeting will be held due to a Houthi attack. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: AI, Robots, and Drones Featured at Astana's AI & Digital Bridge 2026 Exhibition
item.description: Over 100 companies from Kazakhstan and abroad showcased developments at the AI & Digital Bridge 2026 exhibition in Astana. Highlights included humanoid robots, robot dogs, AI-based interactive technologies, drone races, and digital creative industry projects. Technologies spanned medicine, fintech, education, and cybersecurity.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Over 500 Million Tenge Paid to Patients Under Medical Insurance
item.description: In Kazakhstan, 502.6 million tenge has been paid to patients and their families under mandatory insurance for medical professionals' liability over the past two years. The Ministry of Health reported that as of September 1, 2026, 178,296 medical professionals are insured. Since the beginning of 2026, 1,867 insurance contracts have been concluded, with 112 payments made.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Online Environmental Expertise Conclusion Service
item.description: Uzbekistan has launched an online service for obtaining environmental expertise conclusions. The cost of this service varies depending on the project type, potentially reaching up to 11 million Uzbek soums.

item.title: Fire on the roof of a five-story building in Kъonayev extinguished, 120 evacuated
item.description: Firefighters have extinguished a fire on the roof of a five-story residential building in Kъonayev. 120 people, including 30 children, were evacuated from the building. No injuries were reported. The fire was reported to the emergency services and spread to the roof upon arrival of the first units.

item.title: Fire in a multi-story building in Kъonayev, 120 people evacuated
item.description: A fire broke out in the roof of a five-story residential building in Kъonayev, prompting the evacuation of 120 people, including 30 children. Emergency services responded quickly, and firefighters worked to extinguish the blaze. The fire was fully extinguished, and no one was injured.

item.title: Kyiv Bridge Damaged in Russian Attack Shortly After German Chancellor's Arrival
item.description: A bridge in Kyiv was damaged by a Russian attack shortly after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in the city. Emergency services were dispatched to the scene. Merz is in Kyiv for an unannounced visit to discuss defense cooperation and German support, including significant military and energy reconstruction aid.

item.title: Latvian Prime Minister's Party Wins Election with Best Result in 35 Years
item.description: The party of Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kūlbergs secured 35.3% of the vote in parliamentary elections, potentially winning 42 seats in the 100-member Saeima. This marks the largest victory since the country's independence in 1991. Kūlbergs aims to form a coalition supporting Ukraine and maintain a firm stance against Moscow, emphasizing economic ties with Russia weaken the nation.

item.title: Afghanistan's Minister: Unjustified Shedding of Afghan or Pakistani Blood is Forbidden
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Rural Rehabilitation and Development, Abdul Latif Mansour, stated that the Islamic Emirate considers the unjustified shedding of Afghan and Pakistani blood forbidden, as both are Muslim nations. Speaking at the Wakhan road inauguration, Mansour urged self-reliance for Afghanistan to defend its citizens and stressed that the situation should not escalate into indiscriminate bloodshed.

item.title: Kazakhstan Paid Over 500 Million Tenge for Medical Errors in Two Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has paid 502.6 million tenge to patients and their families over the past two years as insurance payouts for medical errors, according to the Ministry of Health. The law on professional liability insurance for medical workers, effective since October 2024, covers 178,296 medical professionals. The mechanism allows patients to receive compensation for harm caused during medical care.

item.title: Kazakh scientist delivers lecture at Cambridge University on ancient Eurasian cultures
item.description: A Kazakh scientist presented findings on ancient Eurasian cultural ties at Cambridge University. The lecture focused on stone sculptures and the Botai culture, highlighting Kazakhstan's archaeological heritage.

item.title: Uzbekistan conference addresses legal literacy and free legal aid for persons with disabilities
item.description: A conference in Tashkent discussed challenges and solutions in enhancing legal literacy and providing free legal aid to persons with disabilities in Uzbekistan. Representatives from NGOs participated.

item.title: Afghanistan inaugurates 121 km Wakhan road connecting to China border
item.description: Afghanistan has inaugurated a 121-kilometer road in the Wakhan Corridor, extending to the border with China. Officials described the project as politically, strategically, and economically significant.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Over 500 Million Tenge Paid in Compensation for Medical Errors
item.description: In Kazakhstan, over 502.6 million tenge has been paid in insurance compensation to patients and their families under mandatory insurance for the professional liability of medical workers. The law, developed on the president's instructions, came into force in October 2024. As of September 1, 2026, 178,296 medical workers are insured.

item.title: US Expels Two Iranian Diplomats After UN General Assembly Stay
item.description: The United States has expelled two Iranian diplomats who remained in the country after the UN General Assembly concluded. The State Department had requested their immediate departure. The expulsions come amid heightened tensions between the US and Iran, complicating diplomatic efforts.

item.title: Ukraine Strikes Belgorod, Russia: One Dead, Several Injured
item.description: Ukrainian forces struck the Russian city and region of Belgorod on October 3, resulting in one death and several injuries, according to Belgorod Governor Alexander Shuvaev. Authorities reported another fatality in the city of Graivoron. In total, 12 people were injured in the Belgorod, Graivoron, and Shebekino areas in the last 24 hours, including four children.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Halts Construction of Most Expensive Stadium for 2034 World Cup Amidst Regional Conflicts
item.description: Saudi Arabia has paused the construction of its most expensive stadium, planned for the 2034 World Cup. This decision is influenced by several factors, including regional conflicts like Houthi attacks impacting logistics and energy exports. The Finance Ministry also anticipates a larger budget deficit this year due to oil sector declines, projecting a 3.6% GDP contraction.

item.title: Taliban Governor in Badakhshan Warns of Death for Opposition to Regime
item.description: The Taliban governor of Badakhshan, Rahmatullah Najib, has issued a stern warning: anyone acting against the group's regime will be killed or captured. He made these remarks during the inauguration of a road in the Wakhan corridor. This statement comes amid reports of opposition presence in Badakhshan and recent clashes.

item.title: Iran Reports Arrests of 31 Individuals Linked to US and Israel
item.description: Iran's Ministry of Intelligence announced the arrest of 31 people allegedly linked to the United States and Israel. The ministry claimed the individuals were apprehended in Kerman province and that "large quantities of Molotov cocktails" were seized. This follows earlier arrests of hundreds on espionage charges after last winter's protests, with some facing execution.

item.title: New Power Transmission Line to be Built from Samarkand to Tashkent
item.description: A new power transmission line will be constructed connecting Samarkand to Tashkent, passing through the regions of Samarkand, Jizzakh, Sirdaryo, and Tashkent. This line will utilize new-design 500 kV double-circuit transmission towers, a first in Central Asia.

item.title: Sofreh Capital Founder Plans to Open Offices in Kazakhstan, Invest in AI Economy
item.description: Sherwin Pishevar, founder of Sofreh Capital, announced plans to open company offices in Kazakhstan, relocate his team, and invest in the local AI economy. He cited Kazakhstan's engineering talent, government support for innovation, and natural resources as attractive factors.

item.title: Iraq Exports Two Million Barrels of Crude Oil Via Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iraq's state-owned Oil Tankers Company has exported two million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz using a very large crude carrier. This move provides greater flexibility for Iraq's State Organization for Marketing of Oil (SOMO) in selling crude. The company obtained Iran's permission for passage.

item.title: Traffic Accident in Nangarhar Claims Lives of Three Family Members
item.description: A traffic accident in the Batikot district of Nangarhar province has resulted in the deaths of three members of a family and injured three others, according to the Taliban's provincial security command. The incident involved two vehicles and occurred around 11:00 AM. The injured were transported to the hospital for treatment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Pays Over 502 Million Tenge in Compensation for Medical Harm
item.description: In Kazakhstan, patients who suffer harm during medical treatment can receive compensation from insurance companies. Over the past two years, 502.6 million tenge has been paid to patients and their families under this mechanism. The system, operational since October 2024, covers 178,296 medical professionals. Claims are reviewed by an independent expert commission.

item.title: Latvia's Interior Ministry Proposes Visa Restrictions for Uzbek Citizens
item.description: Latvia's Ministry of Interior has proposed a temporary suspension of visa issuance to citizens of Uzbekistan, citing an increase in crimes committed by Uzbek nationals, including offenses against minors. The ministry intends to use this period to enhance cooperation with Uzbekistan and strengthen screening of applicants.

item.title: Iran Ready for Military Action if US Chooses Path, Says Foreign Minister
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran is more prepared than ever if the US opts for military action again. He expressed hope for a rational approach from the US but affirmed readiness to defend Iran. Araghchi also noted that new sanctions would be ineffective, advocating for a negotiated solution based on justice.

item.title: Sofreh Capital Founder Plans to Open Company Offices in Kazakhstan
item.description: Sherwin Pishevar, founder and CEO of Sofreh Capital, intends to open company offices in Kazakhstan, relocate part of his team, and begin investing in the country's future. He highlighted Kazakhstan's potential in AI development, citing its engineering talent, state support for innovation, and resource base.

item.title: Shadowy "Fixer" of Akorda: How Nurtleu Outmaneuvered Tokayev's Nephews for Investor Influence
item.description: Whispers in Astana suggest a power struggle within the president's inner circle, with aide Murat Nurtleu reportedly outmaneuvering President Tokayev's nephews for control over foreign investors. The report also touches on the new defense minister's lobbyists and traffic privileges for an Almaty police colonel.

item.title: Kazakhstan Aims to Systematically Develop All Five Levels of Artificial Intelligence Economy
item.description: Kazakhstan intends to systematically develop all five levels of the AI economy, from energy infrastructure and chips to language models and applications, according to Deputy Prime Minister Zhaslan Madiev. The global AI market is valued at over $50 trillion, presenting a significant opportunity for Kazakhstan to secure its place in the new global economy and maximize AI development benefits.

item.title: UN OCHA Calls for Sustainable Funding and Women's Participation in Afghanistan Aid Efforts
item.description: Amy Martin, head of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) in Afghanistan, has urged for sustainable funding, humanitarian access, and meaningful participation of women in aid delivery. Speaking at a European Parliament exhibition, Martin highlighted the challenges in reaching those in need and stressed that continued assistance requires consistent financial support and access.

item.title: Almaty Plans New Transport Projects to Alleviate Traffic Congestion
item.description: Almaty is implementing transport projects including ring lines, transfer hubs, and SkyTrain to create a new rail model. This aims to redistribute passenger flow, reduce traffic on busy routes, and improve urban mobility's environmental impact. The integrated system will connect metro, LRT, and SkyTrain, with future extensions planned.

item.title: Taliban Deputy Intelligence Chief in Faizabad Killed in Attack
item.description: The National Resistance Front of Afghanistan announced that the Taliban's deputy intelligence chief for Faizabad, Badakhshan, was killed along with two guards. The front stated its forces targeted the official on Sunday, October 4, around 9:30 a.m. in the city's sixth district.

item.title: Kazakhstan to disconnect internet for subscribers failing to fix cyber incidents within 48 hours of SMS
item.description: Kazakhstan will disconnect internet services for subscribers who do not resolve cyber incidents within 48 hours after receiving an SMS notification. This measure aims to enhance cybersecurity and prompt response to threats.

item.title: Taliban Inaugurate First Transit Road Between Badakhshan and China
item.description: The Taliban announced the completion and inauguration of the first transit road connecting Afghanistan's Badakhshan province to China's Xinjiang region. The 121-kilometer unpaved road, built by the Ministry of Rural Rehabilitation and Development, aims to facilitate land transit between the two countries.

item.title: UNICEF Highlights Children's Need for Access to Safe Drinking Water
item.description: UNICEF, with support from South Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, is working to improve children's access to safe water and prevent waterborne diseases. The agency noted that some children travel long distances to collect unsafe water, emphasizing that access to clean water saves lives.

item.title: Almaty Seismic Audit Identifies 2,834 Structures Unfit for Earthquakes
item.description: A seismic audit in Almaty has identified 2,834 structures, including 51 multi-story residential buildings housing approximately 2,100 people, that may not withstand strong earthquakes. The audit, conducted in two phases (2017-2018 and 2023-2024), assessed the seismic resistance of buildings. A list of vulnerable facilities has been compiled.

item.title: Ukraine to possess long-range ballistic missile by autumn, says Zelensky
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will have its own long-range ballistic missile by autumn. He has urged the missile developer, Fire Point, to accelerate work on the FP-9 missile, which is expected to be ready this fall. Zelensky previously reported the first combat use of the FP-7 tactical ballistic missile in October.

item.title: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Previously Detained for Extremist Materials, Investigated for Attempted Crash
item.description: The co-pilot of a FlyDubai flight to Tel Aviv, identified as Hamam Al-Hammami, was previously detained in 2024 for possessing extremist materials while training with Oman Air. He was suspended from flying for a year but continued in an administrative role. Investigators are determining how he regained flight privileges.
